title: response from predict()?
description:
What do you guys think about a feature from predict() for bring up the outcome columns as well? Like `predict(workflow_fit_obj, test_data, type = "prob", outcomes = TRUE)`

Once I had a recipe that would do tons of transformations on the outcome and the code to retrieve it in the test step became kinda verbose.

```
# not reproducible! 
my_predict <- function(workflow_fit_obj) {

  outcome <- workflow_fit_obj %>% 
    extract_recipe() %>% 
    bake(new_data) %>%
    pull(outcome_var)
  
  predict(workflow_fit_obj, new_data) %>% 
    mutate(truth = outcome)
}
```

And I guess it would be a widely used feature because one wants to calculate metrics in test data pretty often.
Btw, it woul also spare some computations once predict() already runs recipes::bake()!

title: Error with predict() when a recipe step targets the outcome
description:
After fitting a model using workflows with a recipe that has a step targeting the outcome column, predictions fail with a message indicating a problem with the outcome variable.

Here is a reprex.

```R
# Packages ----
library(magrittr)
library(rsample)
library(recipes)
library(parsnip)
library(workflows)

# Data ----

data(diamonds, package='ggplot2')

# Data Split ----

data_split <- initial_split(diamonds, prop=0.8, strata='price')
train <- training(data_split)
test <- testing(data_split)

# Preprocess

rec1 <- recipe(price ~ carat + x, data=train) %>% 
    step_center(all_outcomes())
prep1 <- prep(rec1, training=train)

# Model Specification ----

net_spec <- linear_reg(penalty=0.645) %>% set_engine('glmnet')

# Workflow ----

flow1 <- workflow() %>% 
    add_recipe(rec1) %>% 
    add_model(net_spec)

# Fit Model ----

mod1 <- flow1 %>% fit(train)

# Predictions ----

# Causes Error
preds1 <- predict(mod1, new_data=test)
# Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
# x The column `price` doesn't exist.
```
Running `rlang::last_error()` tracks this down to `{vctrs}`.

```R
rlang::last_error()
# <error/vctrs_error_subscript_oob>
#     Can't subset columns that don't exist.
# x The column `price` doesn't exist.
# Backtrace:
#   1. stats::predict(mod1, new_data = test)
#  32. vctrs:::stop_subscript_oob(...)
#  33. vctrs:::stop_subscript(...)
# Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see the full context.
```

Yes, this occurs when there is more than one step. I have a feeling this is because somewhere during forging the outcome is removed.

In fact, in `hardhat:::forge.data.frame()`, the line 

```R
cleaned <- blueprint$forge$clean(blueprint = blueprint, new_data = new_data, outcomes = outcomes)
```

eliminates the outcome variable because `outcomes=FALSE` is set. So

```R
outcomes <- cleaned$outcomes
```

is `NULL`.

Then

```R
processed <- blueprint$forge$process(blueprint = blueprint, 
        predictors = predictors, outcomes = outcomes, extras = extras)
```

fails because there is no outcome even though it is not skipping the recipe step that handles the outcome.

Here is the line in `blueprint$forge$process()` that calls the recipe.

```R
baked_data <- recipes::bake(object = rec, new_data = new_data)
```

The recipe looks like this.

```R
rec
Data Recipe

Inputs:

      role #variables
   outcome          1
 predictor          2

Training data contained 43156 data points and no missing data.

Operations:

Centering for price [trained]
```

title: Error in pkg_list[[1]] : subscript out of bounds
description:
I'm working on developing an experimental package, `modeltime`, that ports some of the time series models into the `tidymodels` framework. 

## Problem Statement
When trying to run `tune_grid()` on a `workflow`, I get:
`Error in pkg_list[[1]] : subscript out of bounds`

Any idea why this might be?


## Reproducible Example

Make sure you use the development versions of `timetk` and `modeltime`. 

```
library(tidyverse)
library(parsnip)
library(rsample)
library(recipes)
library(tune)
library(dials)
library(yardstick)
library(workflows)

library(modeltime) # devtools::install_github("business-science/modeltime")
library(timetk)    # devtools::install_github("business-science/timetk")

# DATA ----

m750 <- m4_monthly %>% filter(id == "M750")

# RESAMPLE SPEC ----
resample_spec <- time_series_cv(data = m750,
                                initial     = "6 years",
                                assess      = "2 years",
                                skip        = "2 years",
                                cumulative  = FALSE,
                                slice_limit = 2)

# ARIMA SPEC ----

model_spec <- arima_reg(
    period = 12,
    p = 1, d = tune(), q = 1,
    P = 0, D = 0, Q = 0
) %>%
    set_engine("forecast")


# RECIPE SPEC ----
recipe_spec <- recipe(value ~ date, data = m750)

# WORKFLOW ----

workflow() %>%
    add_recipe(recipe_spec) %>%
    add_model(model_spec) %>%
    tune_grid(
        resamples = resample_spec,
        grid = 2
    )
```

title: tuning fails when recipe step affects an outcome with skip = TRUE
description:
When a recipe step affects an outcome, it must have `skip = TRUE` in order for `predict()` to succeed on the eventual fitted workflow. This has been discussed in several issues here, e.g. [this one](https://github.com/tidymodels/workflows/issues/31).

However, doing that causes `tune` to incorrectly compute metrics like rmse. See [Athospd's reprex here](https://github.com/tidymodels/hardhat/issues/129#issuecomment-626386670).

If this is as intended, is there a recommended approach to tuning such a workflow, fitting the tuned workflow, then predicting on new data?

title: Workflow does not seem to respect steps
description:

Interestingly, using the formula interface and passing the preprocessed data directly does not suffer from this problem. Is this a bug, or am I using the workflow interface incorrectly?

``` r
adult <- ucidata::adult

adult_test  <- testing(adult_split)

  # impute missing values
  step_knnimpute(workclass, neighbors = 5) %>% 
  # collapse levels to remove low-frequency levels

  set_engine('glm')

  add_recipe(adult_rec) %>% 
  add_model(log_mod)

f_wfl <- fit(log_wfl, data = adult_train)
```

title: fit_resample with glm and formula leads to rank deficient design matrix
description:
## The problem

Fitting a `logistic_reg() %>% set_engine("glm")` model on resamples using the model_spec + formula interface of `fit_resamples` leads to a `! FoldXX: model (predictions): prediction from a rank-deficient fit may be misleading` warning.

I believe this is due to the way that a mold is generated from the formula. This is done via a call to `workflows::add_formula()`, which by default sets the intercept to false and indicators to true in the underlying blueprint.

https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/e3189ec07e45bb5748c0c3908905f8e834419cc2/R/resample.R#L113

``` r
workflows::add_formula(workflows::workflow(), y ~ x)$pre$actions$formula$blueprint
#> Formula blueprint: 
#>  
#> # Predictors: 0 
#>   # Outcomes: 0 
#>    Intercept: FALSE       <--
#> Novel Levels: FALSE 
#>   Indicators: TRUE        <--
```

This leads to a mold that explicitely encodes a 2-level factor as a dummy variable in the latter call to

https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/e3189ec07e45bb5748c0c3908905f8e834419cc2/R/resample.R#L319
 
This appears to clash with the function `parsnip:::convert_xy_to_form_fit()` in  `parsnip:::xy_form()`, which is called by

https://github.com/tidymodels/tune/blob/e3189ec07e45bb5748c0c3908905f8e834419cc2/R/resample.R#L338

This reintroduces the formula interface `..y ~ .` which for GLM's adds an intercept by default, leading to a rank-deficient design matrix.

## Reproducible example

``` r
library(rsample)
library(parsnip)
library(tune)

set.seed(123)
n <- 200
x <- sample(0:1, n, replace = TRUE)
y <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.25 + 0.5 * x)

data <- data.frame(
  x = factor(x, 0:1), 
  y = factor(y, 0:1)
)

rs <- vfold_cv(data, v = 2)
model <- logistic_reg("classification") %>% set_engine("glm")
fitted <- fit_resamples(model, y ~ x, rs) 
#> ! Fold1: model (predictions): prediction from a rank-deficient fit may be misleading
#> ! Fold2: model (predictions): prediction from a rank-deficient fit may be misleading
```

description:
Firstly, I do not have a set of code to show my situation.  This is basically a question. Apologies if it has been answered and I have not read it just yet.

Basically, I am working on a classification project using Tidymodels.

I have split the data, set some recipes, established the model, performed the resampling and tune method and have finalised the workflow.  I will be using the workflow to predict future data and I want to be able to save the finalised model to disc/server and then load it as if I were loading a CSV. 

That way when I have users load data to get a prediction, they just wait for the prediction and not for the fit and all the other steps that happen before.


Is this currently possible?

Thanks

title: workflows predict.workflow, hardhat forge and Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist. when recipe includes outcome variables.
description:
Hi folks,
It looks like the `predict` method for `workflow` objects (`workflows:::predict.workflows`) seems to remove the outcome variables in `hardhat::forge`, and thus causes an error if a recipe has a pre-processing step that involves the outcome variables.
I'm cross-posting this to `hardhat` since I think the issue may be in the way variables are passed inside of `hardhat:::forge.data.frame`.

Here's a reprex:
```
test <- setNames(as.data.frame(matrix(rnorm(1000), ncol = 10)), c("y", paste0("x", 1:9)))
rec <- recipes::recipe(y ~ ., data = test) %>% 
  recipes::step_normalize(recipes::all_outcomes())
xgboost = workflows::workflow() %>% 
  workflows::add_recipe(rec) %>% 
  workflows::add_model(
    parsnip::boost_tree(
      mode = "regression",
      mtry = 8,
      trees = 12,
      min_n = 9,
      tree_depth = 8,
      learn_rate = 0.059,
      loss_reduction = 0.0001
    ) %>% 
      parsnip::set_engine("xgboost")
  )         
  fitted <- parsnip::fit(xgboost, test)
  predict(fitted, new_data = test)
  ```
  
Here's the stack trace.
```
1. +-stats::predict(.out, new_data = .d$test)
  2. +-workflows:::predict.workflow(.out, new_data = .d$test)
  3. | +-hardhat::forge(new_data, blueprint)
  4. | \-hardhat:::forge.data.frame(new_data, blueprint)
  5. |   \-blueprint$forge$process(...)
  6. |     +-recipes::bake(object = rec, new_data = new_data)
  7. |     \-recipes:::bake.recipe(object = rec, new_data = new_data)
  8. |       +-recipes::bake(object$steps[[i]], new_data = new_data)
  9. |       \-recipes:::bake.step_normalize(object$steps[[i]], new_data = new_data)
 10. |         +-base::sweep(...)
 11. |         +-base::as.matrix(new_data[, names(object$means)])
 12. |         +-new_data[, names(object$means)]
 13. |         \-tibble:::`[.tbl_df`(new_data, , names(object$means))
 14. |           \-tibble:::vectbl_as_col_location(...)
 15. |             +-tibble:::subclass_col_index_errors(...)
 16. |             | \-base::withCallingHandlers(...)
 17. |             \-vctrs::vec_as_location(j, n, names)
 18. \-vctrs:::stop_subscript_oob(...)
 19.   \-vctrs:::stop_subscript(...)
```
`hardhat::forge` is not passed `outcomes` [predict.R#L59](https://github.com/tidymodels/workflows/blob/2e38caa6868973f9b07f7a5f823f0df80cf55a62/R/predict.R#L59) and thus `hardhat:::forge.data.frame` has `outcomes` as false. When [`blueprint$forge$clean` method](https://github.com/tidymodels/hardhat/blob/c425b289d6ff59ce25b699b11b1ab82ab9da75e0/R/forge.R#L82) is called , `outcome`  is returned as `NULL` even though the `blueprint$recipe$term_info` object still has the `outcome` variable indicated.
 When `blueprint$forge$process` is called and `new_data` is transformed using 
```
new_data <- vctrs::vec_cbind(predictors, outcomes, !!!unname(extras$roles), 
    .name_repair = "minimal")
```
[hardhat::blueprint-recipe-default.R#L341](https://github.com/tidymodels/hardhat/blob/0945426db5978ee5f96d4d27707148205d170a55/R/blueprint-recipe-default.R#L341)
 `new_data` no longer contains the outcome variable. A few steps later when `new_data` reaches the `bake` step, if the recipe involves pre-processing of`outcome` variables, the following error is thrown:
`Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.`

That's the extent of what I can make of it from debugging. 

Hope it's an easy fix!

title: Weird results when a prepped recipe is added to workflow
description:
I'm not very well versed in the internals of workflows. But is there a reason why we allow a prepped recipe to be passed in via `add_recipe()`?

``` r
library(recipes)
library(tidymodels)

set.seed(212)

circle_example2 <- themis::circle_example %>%
  mutate(category = rep(c("A", "B"), length.out = n())) %>%
  as_tibble()

processed_recipe <-
  recipe(class ~ ., data = circle_example2) %>%

spec <- null_model() %>% 
  set_engine("parsnip")

wflow <-
  workflow() %>%
  add_recipe(processed_recipe) %>%
  add_model(spec) %>%
  fit(data = circle_example2)

prepped <- prep(processed_recipe)

wflow <-
```

title: Unexpected behaviour when using workflow with a recipe preprocesser scaling the outcome variable
description:
Hi, as with my recent issues on [TMwR](https://github.com/tidymodels/TMwR) I am currently going through the current version of the book to get a better understanding of the package universe. 

This time I've come across a possible bug (or curiosity) with the workflow integration with `recipes` in [chapter 8.3](https://www.tmwr.org/workflows.html#workflows-and-recipes). In the example the `ames` dataset is used to fit a simple linear regression. In this process `Sale_Price` is log transformed before being handed to the recipe, and then we predict a bit of data as described in [chapter 7.5](https://www.tmwr.org/models.html#models-summary). A slightly reduces example is provided below.

```R

library(tidymodels)
data(ames, package = "modeldata")
```

description:
## The problem

I'm trying to get a multinomial model estimated using `workflows`, `recipes` and `parsnip` but at some point it would appear the predictors are removed when it comes time to fit the model.

After running the above, the `parsnip::fit` step returns the following error:
> Error in glmnet::glmnet(x = maybe_matrix(x), y = y, family = "multinomial") : 
>   x should be a matrix with 2 or more columns
> Timing stopped at: 0 0 0

## Reproducible example

I've put together a toy example with `mtcars`. I modified variable `carb` to be used as a test outcome factor. I then follow the typical approach for creating a multinomial model via `parsnip`, a recipe where I specify roles, and a workflow to bring them all together. I appreciate this model makes no sense but I'm looking to confirm the code and process are sound so I can apply it to models that actually make sense.

```r
library(magrittr)

mod_d <- mtcars %>%
  dplyr::select(carb, mpg, disp, hp, drat) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(carb = carb %>% 
                  # recode levels 6 and 8 to 3 for testing purposes
                  # multinomial models require more than one observation 
                  # per outcome class
                  dplyr::if_else(. %in% c(6, 8), 3, .) %>% 
                  as.factor)

  parsnip::set_engine('glmnet') %>%
  parsnip::set_mode('classification')

recipe_d <- mod_d %>%
  recipes::recipe() %>%
  recipes::update_role(carb, new_role = 'outcome') %>%
  recipes::update_role(mpg, disp, hp, drat, new_role = 'predictors')
```

title: add variables and special model formulas
description:
With upcoming hierarchical models, GAMS, and others, we need to make the workflow interface smoother. 

Currently, it is not intuitive in a few ways: 

 * There are the usual formula and the model formula (that you get via `add_model()`). 
 * The default formula processing can eliminate the specific variables that you want to keep intact. 

Historically, the model formula has always done many things: specify the variables in the model, create encodings for them, and then hand them off to the model with the appropriate analysis roles (e.g. outcome, predictor, etc). 

## Example

For example, if there was a `parsnip` hierarchical model to fit via stan or `lme4`, a user's initial stab would be: 

```r
library(tidymodels)

data(sleepstudy, package = "lme4")

mod <- linear_reg() %>% set_engine("stan glmer")

wflow_0 <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  # Won't work since the basic formula method makes dummy variables
  add_formula(Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject)) %>% 
  add_model(mod)
````

`fit()` will generate the error: 

```
Error in Days || Subject : invalid 'y' type in 'x || y'
```

(which could be better)


Looking around, the `formula` argument to `add_model()` is found: 

```r
wflow_1 <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  # Make a simple formula for processing the data 
  add_formula(Reaction ~ Days + Subject) %>% 
  # Then add another formula to give to the model: 
  add_model(mod, formula = Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject))
````

That ends in an error of 

```
Error in eval(predvars, data, env) : object 'Subject' not found 
``` 
because `add_formula()` makes dummy variables. 

## Current solution

After searching a lot more, there are two options that are kludgy but work:

```r
bp <- hardhat::default_formula_blueprint(indicators = FALSE)
wflow_2 <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  add_formula(Reaction ~ ., blueprint = bp) %>% 
  add_model(mod, formula = Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject))

wflow_3 <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  add_recipe(recipe(Reaction ~ ., data = sleepstudy)) %>% 
  add_model(mod, formula = Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject))
```

We can make this interface a lot better and intuitive.

## Proposals

Some straw-man proposals:

First, let's make a function where users can tell the model what data to use, and maybe their limited roles, without doing any pre-processing: 

```r
wflow_4 <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  # Add in the data by processing through only `model.frame()` or equivalent. 
  # No other in-line functions used; just as-is:
  add_variables_asis(Reaction ~ .) %>% 
  add_model(mod, formula = Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject))
```

Having two formulas might be confusing. Basic `tidyselect` tools could be used instead: 

```r
wflow_5 <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  # If formulas are confusing, we could use tidyselect functions
  add_variables(one_of(Reaction, Days, Subject)) %>% 
  add_model(mod, formula = Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject))
```

Even though the endpoint could be achieved using current code, the existing methods are not intuitive and also not well documented in `workflows`. 

Second, even though the model formula is tied to the model, it might be better to have a separate _add_ function that attaches a model formula to a model specification: 

```r
wflow_6 <- 
  workflow() %>% 
  add_variables(one_of(Reaction, Days, Subject)) %>% 
  add_model(mod) %>% 
  add_model_formula(Reaction ~ Days + (Days || Subject))
```

A few people might want to add input: @jaredlander, @beckmart, @monicathieu, @billdenney, @emitanaka, and @Athanasiamo

title: Uninformative error if predictors are specified wrongly in add_variables()
description:
I'm not quite sure if this is a workflows issue or tidyselect issue.

If you are not quite familiar with the tidyselect way of doing things you might try to specify predictors as you do in formula expressions. 

Maybe a simple check and to see if `+` is used would be sufficient

``` r
library(workflows)
library(parsnip)

spec_lm <- linear_reg() %>%
  set_engine("lm")

workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(spec_lm) %>%
  add_variables(
    outcomes = mpg,
    predictors = cyl + disp
  )

fit(workflow, mtcars)
#> Error: object 'cyl' not found
```
